Formula: Binomial Theorem
Exact Expression: (x + y)^n = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} x^{n-k} y^k
Definitions: Algebraic expansion of powers of a binomial into a polynomial sum with combinatorial coefficients.
Derivation/Reference: Pingala Chanda Sutra (Meru Prastara, c. 200 BCE); Isaac Newton generalized to real/complex exponents (1665)
Example: (x + y)^3 = x^3 + 3x^2 y + 3xy^2 + y^3 where binom(3, 1) = 3!/(1!2!) = 3
Domain: combinatorics
Assumptions: n in Z_{>=0}, xy = yx (commutative ring)
Common Errors: Applying standard finite summation formula to negative or non-integer n without infinite series convergence constraints
subject: Binomial Theorem
